name: 15-the-website
description: The documentation site, tab by tab: the home page, getting started, the catalogs generated from the code, MoonWalk, the tests, and the reference and developer pages.

steps.title: The website
steps.caption: The website. Organized by who reads it.
The home page is the project's README, so GitHub and the website say the same thing: every effect as an animated card, and what MoonLight runs on.
The tabs follow the reader: getting started first, then the pages generated from the code, then reference for users and developers for contributors.
Getting started explains how MoonLight works for you, one card per idea, each with a picture.
Three ways in: flash an ESP32 from your browser, run it on a laptop with no hardware at all, or build it from source.
And for developers: how a change travels from an idea to a release, with every check on the way.
The catalogs are generated from the code itself. Every effect is a card that plays its own preview.
Search narrows the deck as you type.
Modifiers, layouts and drivers work the same way, and so do the services and the system modules.
MoonWalk puts every process on one map: installing, building a show, contributing. The same map opens on the device.
Tests lists every test and every check by subject, with the counts on every branch.
Search finds every test that touches brightness.
Attributions credits the people and projects MoonLight learned from, each with the modules that use their work.
Reference holds what you look up while using it: the hardware, presets, home automation and the REST API.
Developers holds the architecture, the standards, and how the build and the tests work.
And search covers the whole site, every page and every card.
MoonLight's website: what it is, how to use it, and how it is built.
